key_insight: OpenGEM26 is a large DFT-derived molecular dataset that enables a graph neural network force field, GPTFF-mol, to model organic molecules with higher efficiency and strong accuracy beyond QM9-like coverage.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical ML potential for fast atomistic simulation of sulfur- and chlorine-containing organic molecules, supporting conformational search, dynamics, and reaction-barrier studies.
method: Built OpenGEM26 with 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations.
Computed optimized trajectories and non-equilibrium structures using ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP with dispersion corrections.
Trained a graph neural network force field (GPTFF-mol) on H/C/N/O/S/Cl species with up to 10 heavy atoms.
evidence_signal: The dataset spans broader conformational space than QM9 in energy, bond lengths, and bond angles, and GPTFF-mol reaches 16 meV/molecule energy MAE with better force performance than ANI-2x.
watch_item: Model reliability may be limited outside the chemistry and size range covered by OpenGEM26, especially for larger molecules or chemistries not included in training.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
